title: Lights
sub: Ambient, Directional, Point: how each one shines
cards/0/body:
AmbientLight: even light from everywhere. It adds no depth, it just "lifts the shadows".
DirectionalLight: like the sun, parallel rays from one side.
PointLight: a light bulb, shining in all directions and fading with distance.
SpotLight: a spotlight, shining in a cone.
cards/1/task: Only an AmbientLight, so the knot looks flat. Add a bulb to bring out the shape.
cards/2/q: Why does the shape look flat with just an AmbientLight?
cards/2/options/0: It shines equally from every side, so there are no lit and dark sides
cards/2/options/2: It does not work with Standard
cards/2/explain: The eye reads shape from differences in lighting.
cards/3/body: Since r155, lighting in Three.js is physically correct. PointLight and SpotLight have decay = 2: brightness drops with the square of the distance. So a bulb with intensity = 1 five meters from an object barely lights it, and people use values in the tens.
cards/4/q: A PointLight with intensity 1 barely lights an object 5 meters away. Why?
cards/4/options/0: Light fades with distance squared: at 5 m it is 25 times weaker
cards/4/options/1: PointLight does not reach beyond 1 m
cards/4/explain: Raise the intensity or move the light closer.
cards/5/body: A directional light shines from its position toward its target (the world origin by default). You can move the target, but then you have to add it to the scene.
cards/6/q: Match each light to its real-world twin
cards/7/q: A classic, inexpensive lighting setup? Select everything it needs.
cards/7/options/0: A dimmer AmbientLight or HemisphereLight, so shadows are not pitch black
cards/7/options/1: One DirectionalLight as the key light
cards/7/explain: Every light is extra shader work for every pixel.
